CONTEXT. factory/reescalate.py re-pings the owner about a card he has not answered. It exists and its cadence is already tested. It is not yet wired to a systemd timer, and two small things block that. The owner may take days to answer, and the Telegram buttons carry a nonce that dies after 72 hours, so the re-ping is what keeps his buttons alive. If it never runs, 'answer whenever' is a lie.

READ FIRST, READ-ONLY: factory/reescalate.py in full, factory/outbox_push.py for the sender-template convention, and tests/test_reescalate.py for the existing test style.

CHANGE 1. --now must become OPTIONAL, defaulting to the real current UTC time. A systemd service should be able to call this with no shell computing a date. Keep --now working exactly as it does now when supplied, because every existing cadence test depends on injecting a fixed instant.

CHANGE 2. The sender template must also be able to render {department} and {first_raised}, alongside the existing {card_identifier}, {issue}, {reescalation_count}, {reason}, {text} and {now}. The phone notifier needs the department to label the buzz, and the owner needs to see how long an item has been waiting. Take both from the card's latest ledger row; render an empty string when a row genuinely lacks them rather than crashing.

DO NOT CHANGE: the cadence maths, the eligibility rule (only open and fix_requested), the one-ping-per-card rule, the ledger row it appends after a ping (which must keep status unchanged and advance reescalation_count and last_ping_at), or the fail-closed behaviour when the sender config is missing or unusable.

WRITE tests/test_reescalate_timer.py covering: --now omitted works; --now supplied still works; {department} and {first_raised} render; a ping advances reescalation_count and last_ping_at without changing status; and an immediate second run does not double-ping. Your tests are not the acceptance gate; an independent oracle drives the CLI through fixtures you have not seen.

OWNERSHIP: you own exactly two paths, factory/remote_outbox_pull.py (new) and tests/test_remote_outbox_pull.py (new). Do NOT modify, create, delete, or reformat anything else under factory/, tests/, kernel/, runbooks/, departments/, or loopfactory.py. Do NOT git commit or push, do NOT run git add -A. Leave changes uncommitted; the check exports them.

CONTEXT. Agents run on more than one machine. A second machine (a Mac mini running Codex) raises approval packets by appending JSON lines to its own local outbox file. It deliberately holds NO credential: no Linear token, no Telegram token, no ssh key inbound. This box already has outbound ssh access to that machine, so THIS box pulls the packets down. Once a pulled file lands in the right local path, the existing mailroom turns each new line into a Linear card and a phone buzz. You are building only the pull.

READ FIRST, READ-ONLY: factory/outbox_push.py, especially how it uses a cursor keyed by watch path with an offset and recent row hashes, and factory/human_in_the_loop.py for the atomic-write convention used throughout this repo.

BUILD factory/remote_outbox_pull.py with this CLI:
  python3 factory/remote_outbox_pull.py --source <src> --dest <dest> [--ssh-host <user@host>] [--identity <keyfile>]
Behaviour:
1. When --ssh-host is absent, --source is a plain LOCAL path. This mode is not a toy: it is how the puller is verified without a second machine, and the check uses it.
2. When --ssh-host is present, fetch the remote file over ssh or scp using --identity if supplied. Never read, print, or log the contents of the identity file; pass it to the transport only.
3. APPEND-ONLY MERGE. --dest is the file the mailroom watches. Bring across only lines not already present, preserving order. Pulling twice in a row must add nothing. A new remote line must arrive on the next pull.
4. FAIL CLOSED AND NON-DESTRUCTIVE. If the source is unreachable, unreadable, or returns nothing, exit nonzero with a printed reason AND leave --dest exactly as it was. Never truncate, never clobber, never write a partial file into place: build the new content and move it into position atomically. Losing a pulled packet loses a decision the owner never got the chance to make.
5. Skip blank lines. A line that is not valid JSON is a real problem: refuse it loudly rather than passing malformed input to the mailroom.
6. Print a one-line summary of how many rows were added, so a timer log is readable.

WRITE tests/test_remote_outbox_pull.py covering local-source pull, idempotency, incremental arrival, unreachable-source non-destruction, and malformed-line refusal. Use tmp_path and the repo's existing subprocess test style. Your tests are not the acceptance gate; an independent oracle drives the CLI through fixtures you have not seen.

VERIFY from the worktree root: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider. The whole suite must stay green.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: leave the two owned files edited and uncommitted, and write ./notes.md at the ROOT of your worktree recording what you read, what you changed, the exact verification command and its result, and any assumption.

HARD RULES: no new dependencies, no allow-on-failure paths, and no credential ever read or logged. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. Do not capture anything to any memory or brain service.
